questions.stem: A man presented with frequent urination and increased thirst. MRI revealed the absence of the posterior pituitary bright spot. He was initiated on desmopressin which improved his symptoms. The affected structure is derived from:
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario of polyuria and polydipsia along with the investigation findings is suggestive of central diabetes insipidus. It involves the diencephalon, a structure that is derived from the prosencephalon.

The diencephalon forms the thalamus, epithalamus, subthalamus, and hypothalamus.

The MRI given below shows the posterior pituitary bright spot. The arrow points at the posterior pituitary and the arrowhead at the anterior pituitary.

questions.stem: Which of the following is false regarding the anatomical relations of the thalamus?

options.label: A
options.text: Anterior pole of thalamus forms the posterior boundary of the interventricular foramen.

options.label: B
options.text: Pulvinar projects over the superior colliculus.

options.label: C
options.text: Medial surface of thalamus forms the inferior boundary of III ventricle.

options.label: D
options.text: The posterior limb of the internal capsule is laterally related to the thalamus.

questions.answerText: Medial surface of thalamus forms the inferior boundary of III ventricle.
questions.solutionHtml:
The medial surface of the thalamus does not form the inferior boundary of the third ventricle. It forms the lateral wall of the IIIrd ventricle.

The thalamus is an ovoid shape mass of grey matter that forms a relay station for all information passing to the cerebral cortex, basal ganglia, hypothalamus, and brainstem.

Relations of the thalamus: 

  • Anteriorly: Interventricular foramen 
  • Superiorly: It is covered by a sheet of white matter called stratum zonale. Above the stratum zonale lies the body of fornix and the ventricle
  • Posteriorly: The posterior end is expanded to form the pulvinar, which overhangs above the superior colliculus. 
  • Inferiorly: Plane connecting the hypothalamic sulci


  • Medially: Lateral wall of the third ventricle 
  • Laterally: Posterior limb of the internal capsule

The image below demonstrates the lateral and medial relations of the thalamus.








Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no. 350

questions.stemHtml: The following section of the brain is given to you. Which of the following is true about the marked structure?

options.label: A
options.text: The external medullary lamina is a sheet of grey matter on the lateral surface of thalamus.

options.label: B
options.text: The intralaminar nuclei lie outside the internal medullary lamina.

options.label: C
options.text: The internal medullary lamina divides the thalamus into three parts.

options.label: D
options.text: The internal medullary lamina divides the thalamus into two parts.

questions.answerText: The internal medullary lamina divides the thalamus into three parts.
questions.solutionHtml:
The marked structure ‘X’ is thalamus. Internal medullary lamina is a Y-shaped sheet of white matter dividing the thalamus to 3 parts:

  • Anterior nuclear groups
  • Medial nuclear groups
  • Lateral nuclear groups

External medullary lamina is a sheet of white matter on the lateral surface of the thalamus that separates the thalamus from the reticular nucleus.

The intralaminar nuclei lie embedded within the internal medullary lamina and the midline nuclei lie close to the lateral walls of the third ventricle.



The thalamus plays an important role in sensory and motor integration.

Input and output of the thalamus:

  • Pre-cortical input- All sensory system (except olfactory system) 
  • Cerebral cortex input- Largest input (from modified pyramidal cells of layer VI )
  • Projection fibers to other areas-
    • Cerebral cortex (most fibers)
    • Basal nuclei and hypothalamus (few fibers)





Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no. 350

questions.stem: Which of the following is false about the anterior thalamic nuclei?

options.label: A
options.text: Largest subdivison is the anteromedial nucleus

options.label: B
options.text: Receives fibers from the mamillary body

options.label: C
options.text: Lesion on this nuclei can cause amnesia

options.label: D
options.text: Involved in regulation of alertness and attention

questions.answerText: Largest subdivison is the anteromedial nucleus
questions.solutionHtml:
The largest subdivision of anterior thalamic nuclei is the anteroventral nucleus (and not the anteromedial nucleus). 

The anterior thalamic nuclei have 3 subdivisions—anteroventral nucleus, anteromedial nucleus and anterodorsal nucleus.

  • Major input: Mamillothalamic tract from the mammillary nuclei of the hypothalamus.
  • Major cortical output: Anterior limbic area, cingulate, and the parahippocampal gyrus 
  • Major function:
    • Regulation of alertness and attention
    • Acquisition of memory

 





Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no. 351

questions.stem: The medial nucleus of the thalamus predominantly receives input from the ____ and sends output to the _____.
questions.solutionHtml:
The medial nucleus of the thalamus predominantly receives input from the hypothalamus and sends output to the prefrontal cortex.

The medial thalamic nuclei contain the large dorsomedial nucleus and several smaller nuclei:

  • Internally, the dorsomedial nucleus is connected to all other thalamic nuclei.
  • Externally, it has 2 major connections—the prefrontal cortex and the hypothalamus. Its functions include integration of somatic, visceral, and olfactory sensory information as well as relation of this sensory information to emotional feelings and subjective states.




Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy, 8th edition, Page no. 365

questions.stem: Choose the incorrect statement with respect to thalamic nuclei.

options.label: A
options.text: Intralaminar nuclei influences the levels of consciousness

options.label: B
options.text: Medial geniculate body receives information from both the ears, but predominantly from contralateral ear

options.label: C
options.text: Lateral geniculate body receives visual information from opposite field of vision

options.label: D
options.text: Medial geniculate body receives information from both the ears, but predominantly from ipsilateral ear

questions.answerText: Medial geniculate body receives information from both the ears, but predominantly from ipsilateral ear
questions.solutionHtml:
The medial geniculate body receives auditory input from both the ears, but predominantly from the contralateral ear (not ipsilateral ear).

questions.stemHtml: MRI of the coronal section of the brain is given to you. Which of the following nuclei of the marked structure does not project to neocortex?
questions.solutionHtml:
The marked structure is the thalamus. The reticular nucleus of the thalamus does not project to the neocortex. Its output is mainly to the other thalamic nuclei.

All other thalamic nuclei send output to the neocortex.





Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy, 8th edition, Page no. 366

questions.stem: A man sustained a head injury 6 weeks back, following a road traffic accident. Now, he complains of increased frequency of urination and excessive thirst. An injury to which nucleus is likely to cause the given condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lesion of the supraoptic nucleus of the hypothalamus causes inhibition of the synthesis of vasopressin leading to diabetes insipidus.

The hypothalamus is a part of the diencephalon that lies below the thalamus. 

  • Anteriorly, the preoptic area is included in the hypothalamus.
  • Posteriorly, it merges with the tegmentum of the midbrain.
  • Laterally, it is bounded by the internal capsule.

Microscopically, the hypothalamus is divided into multiple nuclei.





Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy, 8th edition, Page no. 380

questions.stem: What structure is not a part of the epithalamus?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tuber cinereum is not a part of the epithalamus. It is a part of the hypothalamus.

The epithalamus consists of:

  • Anterior and posterior paraventricular nuclei
  • Medial and lateral habenular nuclei
  • Stria medullaris thalami
  • Posterior commissure 
  • Pineal gland




Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no. 362

questions.stemHtml: A woman with right-sided loss of sensations of both the upper and lower limb complains of shooting pain from her fingers to the right shoulder and a burning sensation when touching cold water. Motor functions are normal. Which of the following structures is likely to be involved?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical stem of a hemi-sensory loss and severe excruciating pain of the affected areas is suggestive of thalamic pain syndrome also known as Dejerine Roussy syndrome. Hence, thalamus marked as B is most likely to be involved.

Occlusion of these thalamic and thalamogeniculate branches results in the thalamic pain syndrome. It is characterized by C/L hemisensory loss which starts as numbness and progresses to cause severe burning pain in the affected regions. As the thalamus is the site for the relay of sensory information between the periphery and cortex, a lesion in the thalamus causes a miscommunication between the afferent pathway and cortex of the brain. Pain occurs during the recovery from the thalamic infarct. This pain responds poorly to analgesics. Anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine or gabapentin or tricyclic antidepressants may be beneficial.

Other markings:

A: Caudate nucleus

C: Substantia nigra

D: Pons
